items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: Terry Gibbs told me that whatever Charlie Parker played, fast or slow, it was always a song.

ctx.x: They don’t know what I mean.

No Chick got me on the phone and he talked to me for 20 minutes about melody. I was surprised. Okay? His philosophy on melody. Playing the melody. In fact when I did the first take on “Skylark” I did a lot of embellishments. And he said, “Glenn, that’s a beautiful tune, Hoagie Carmichael. Please play the melody on the first chorus.” I was surprised. And I felt like saying, “You’re telling me to play the melody? Did you ever listen to yourself?” But he has a beautiful viewpoint on melody, he really does. And he is…
Are there a couple of things that you can relate to people that define a good and memorable melody?
